text: Why can no program compute K(s)?
choices: Because computing K requires running every program, and some do not halt.
Because K depends on the language, and no program can enumerate all languages.
Because the search would never terminate, since high-complexity strings may not exist.
A short program searching for the first string with K(s) > n would itself be a short description of a string that by definition has none.
explanation: The searching program has length about c + log₂ n, which gives K(s) ≤ c + log₂ n while the search guaranteed K(s) > n — false for large n. The search does terminate, because most strings of length n+1 have complexity above n. It is the Berry paradox made rigorous, and it is the same shape as `trouble`: a construction that contradicts its own defining property.
